summary: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX, with 1 advisory. The three v2 SHOULD-FIX findings are repaired without regressing the v1 closures. The refusal law now has an explicit type-level complement and a content-level host-validation limb, so malformed or masquerading fact candidates and nonconforming Coverage are operative refusals rather than examples doing unstated work. The exact delivery.v2 TypeScript wire bytes are pinned; applied delivery.v4 is a derivation over that base and changes zero TypeScript-subtree paths. NT-6 restores constructible D9/exit/HostTermination refusal coverage and NT-7 covers planAdmission plus attempted RequestId/ExecutionId allocation. Across NT-1 through NT-7, all eleven named instances have a retained class on a closed-frame, closed-payload, registry-validation, identity-validation, or Coverage-validation surface. The file-01 preview delta remains explicit and exhaustive, the live DR-133 cell is answered in three obligations, and all status and authority denials hold. The sole advisory carries forward the predecessor observation that explicit routing of parked identity dependencies would improve traceability; no v3 claim depends on such a recipe. DR-133 remains OPEN and this verdict authorizes nothing.
